A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ASB research work with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–F. Text and visual comparisons support reliable judgments throughout.

before.justification: v2 reports original ASB experiments across 13 LLM backbones, including attack, defense, utility, and supplementary analysis results in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix D, including attack success rates and defense evaluations.

M1.justification: The ReAct framework, attack procedures, PoT backdoor construction, and defenses in Section 4 and Appendix A are unchanged. The CoT-to-PoT correction in Appendix D.2.2 fixes terminology for an existing experiment.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same ten ASB scenarios, agents, task and tool sets, and aggressive/non-aggressive cases documented in Table 3 and Appendix B.

E2.justification: The evaluated attack variants and defense comparators remain identical in the corresponding main and appendix experiments. No comparison method is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: Both retain the same 13 LLM backbones, simulated tool calls, PoT demonstration and testing setup, and seven evaluation metrics. Section 5.2 and Appendix C contain no protocol revisions.

E4.justification: Appendix D retains the same attack-combination, trigger, aggressive/non-aggressive, defense-utility, and detection-threshold analyses. All three Figure 2 panels already appear in v2; the expanded caption adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point estimates and averages. Neither reports repeated-run variability, seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and no uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted observations, and reported findings are unchanged. Table 5 retains Mixed Attack's 84.30% average ASR; Table 20 retains PoT ASR of 42.12% without defense and 29.06% with paraphrasing.

T1.justification: The threat-model assumptions, mathematical definitions, attack and defense formalizations, and metric equations remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about ASB coverage, PoT novelty, the NRP metric, agent vulnerabilities, and limited defense effectiveness.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 retains the capability–vulnerability relationship, refusal-based explanation, and NRP recommendation. Appendix D retains the same mechanism explanations and practical caveats; wording and terminology corrections introduce no substantive interpretation or limitation.

D1.justification: Benchmark construction, implementation settings, prompts, tool simulation, and reproducibility information in Appendices B, C, and F are unchanged. Code and documentation access links also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning against InjecAgent and AgentDojo are unchanged, including Section 2, Appendix B.3, and the bibliography.

P1.justification: Section 5.3 adds explicit Figure 2 references and lightly revises wording, including replacing 'Larger models' with 'Better agents with stronger backbone LLMs.' Appendix D.2.2 corrects 'CoT' to 'PoT.' Section organization is unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2's caption now describes all three existing panels instead of only two. Nearby text and Table 6 shift slightly through reflow, and Appendix C.2.4 removes red highlighting from the trigger example. Plots and table structures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The corrected Figure 2 caption and added panel references improve navigation, while the CoT-to-PoT correction resolves a terminology inconsistency in Appendix D.2.2. These provide a small clarity improvement; the methods, empirical evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged.
